subject: maths
question: A solid sphere of diameter 7 cm is cut into two equal halves. What will be the increase in its total surface area?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a **solid sphere** is cut into two equal halves, the increase in **Total Surface Area (TSA)** is equal to the area of the two new circular faces created.

Increase in TSA = 2 × πr²

Given **Diameter** = 7 cm ⇒ **Radius (r)** = 3.5 cm or 7/2 cm.

Increase = 2 × (22/7) × (7/2) × (7/2) = 77 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 77 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Diameter** of the solid sphere (d) = 7 cm

**Radius** of the solid sphere (r) = d/2 = 7/2 = 3.5 cm

**Formula Used:**

TSA of Sphere = 4πr²

TSA of one Hemisphere = 3πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/033a414d54f4eac142d45e5bde230bc16f67231a48168a9f06e58782f1ffd6b1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Total Surface Area = 4 × π × (7/2)²

⇒ Total Surface Area of two equal hemispheres = 2 × (3 × π × (7/2)²) = 6 × π × (7/2)²

⇒ Increase in Surface Area = (6 × π × (7/2)²) − (4 × π × (7/2)²)

⇒ Increase in Surface Area = 2 × π × (7/2)²

⇒ Increase = 2 × (22/7) × (49/4)

⇒ Increase = (44/7) × (49/4) = 11 × 7

⇒ Increase = 77 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 77 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Surface Area of Sphere

The total surface area of a sphere is 4πr², where r is the radius.

Surface Area of Hemisphere

A hemisphere has a curved surface area (CSA) of 2πr² and a total surface area (TSA) of 3πr² including the flat circular base.

Volume Formulas

Volume of a sphere = (4/3)πr³ and Volume of a hemisphere = (2/3)πr³.

General Cutting Rule

When any solid is cut, the increase in TSA is equal to the sum of the areas of the newly exposed surfaces.</p
